claims.statement: This OIDC cloud guide applies to FPT/GHEC/GHES, while GHES does not support GitHub-hosted runners; OIDC avoids stored long-lived credentials where the provider supports it.
Configure provider trust in the GitHub issuer and workflow authentication as separate steps; token issuance alone grants no cloud role.

The prerequisites require a security strategy and at least one trust condition excluding untrusted repositories. Dependabot dynamic event_name applies on FPT/GHEC and GHES>3.20; GHE.com substitutions apply to GHEC, and both require provider-specific review.
Workflow setup requires token permission plus an official provider action for JWT exchange, or a reviewed manual exchange if none exists.
When environments participate in workflows or OIDC policies, the source recommends environment protection rules, for example restricting branches/tags that may deploy or access environment secrets.
Setting the id-token permission to write permits requesting an OIDC JWT, not modifying repository resources; job-scoped elevation still needs explicit trust and permission review.
An official provider action simplifies JWT exchange; the named Alibaba action is an example, not reviewed installation or authorization.
Custom exchange uses core.getIDToken or the request URL/authorization environment values, then exchanges the JWT with the provider; those request credentials must remain confidential.

The custom github-script example installs a versioned toolkit and puts a JWT in outputs; these illustrative dependencies and credential outputs require source review and safe handling rather than direct template adoption.
The request-token/URL output example exposes sensitive request material and enables debugging; it is an illustration, not a production-safe logging pattern.
The curl example prints, decodes and writes a JWT to outputs; production implementations must reconcile this example with secret-masking and disclosure guidance instead of emitting credentials.
Cloud validation exchanges JWT claims for a provider access token described as job-bounded; no actual token lifetime or effective cloud permission is measured here.
Resource access steps vary by provider, and access-token expiry is configurable in the cloud; review actual lifetime instead of treating job duration as a universal TTL guarantee.
Reusable-workflow and self-hosted-runner further-reading links are navigation, not additional whole-file certification.

scope: Full pinned article and literal closure read; source propositions are reference-only and do not adopt policy.
